newsitem.title: UK: Amersham syringe Myoview approved in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Amersham syringe Myoview approved in Japan.

text.p: British radioactive healthcare specialist Amersham International Plc said on Wednesday that a ready-to-inject form of heart-imaging agent Myoview had been approved for manufacture and sale in Japan.

Myoview, which is used for distinguishing between strokes and heart attacks, will be made and distributed by Amersham's joint venture in Japan with Sumitomo Chemical Co, Nihon Medi-Physics Co Ltd (NMP).
Amersham said in a statement that it expected to launch the ready-to-inject form of Myoview in Japan "early in 1997."

The syringe form of the agent had been developed especially for the Japanese market, Amersham said. A different version of Myoview, which is preferred in the U.S. and Europe, had been on sale there since April 1994.
"This is the last piece of the jigsaw for Myoview, which will now be available in each major region in the form which each local market prefers," Amersham chief executive Bill Castell said.
Japan is a key market for Myoview, accounting for around 30 percent of the world market for radioactive healthcare products.
The launch of ready-to-inject Myoview was a key factor in the formation of the NMP joint venture, which is expected to be finalised later this month when Amersham raises its stake to 50 percent.
The company said it would have taken many years to establish its own manufacturing base for the agent in Japan.
Amersham said the Japan launch would confirm Myoview as "a major competitor in cardiology imaging in each of the world's major healthcare markets, together worth some 250 million stg a year."
Amersham announced in April that it intended to raise its 20 percent stake in NMP, acquired in December 1994, to 50 percent, much earlier than originally intended.
It agreed to pay 51.4 million stg in cash and to transfer its Japanese healthcare business to NMP in return for the remaining stake.
